entries.title: Namespace with no Pod Security enforcement, no NetworkPolicy
entries.why: No PSA label means nothing stops a privileged pod; no policy means a flat network and the cloud metadata API is reachable.

entries.title: Namespace enforcing only 'baseline', ingress-only NetworkPolicy
entries.why: baseline is weaker than restricted; with no egress policy pods can reach 169.254.169.254.

entries.title: Egress policy that allows everything (metadata API still open)
entries.why: An Egress-type policy with a single empty rule admits every destination, including 169.254.169.254. The scanner treats ANY egress policy as blocking the metadata API.
entries.gap_reason: net-metadata-api-open only checks that an Egress-type policy exists, not that it excludes the metadata address
entries.would_detect_with: evaluate egress rules with netpol.py against 169.254.169.254/32

entries.title: The built-in 'default' namespace, left as every cluster ships it
entries.why: Every cluster has one; teams deploy into it by accident.

entries.title: Hardened namespace: PSA restricted + default-deny in both directions
entries.why: Everything a namespace should have.

entries.title: Privileged container
entries.why: Kubernetes requires allowPrivilegeEscalation=true for a privileged container, so the second rule is a genuine consequence.

entries.title: Docker socket mounted
entries.why: The socket is itself a hostPath, so the writable-hostPath rule also applies.

entries.title: Image with no tag at all
Bare privileged Pod (no controller)
entries.why: Same as WL-01 on a standalone Pod.

entries.title: Privileged container in a CronJob (persistence)
entries.why: The pod template sits three levels down in a CronJob.

entries.title: Privileged INIT container
entries.why: An init container is as much a host-escape primitive as a long-running one.

entries.title: Kitchen sink: everything wrong at once
entries.why: Every flaw above in one pod.

entries.title: No securityContext at all
entries.why: With no securityContext the runtime defaults apply, so the other hardening rules are true consequences.

entries.title: Windows HostProcess container (fixture only)
entries.why: A Linux cluster rejects this pod, so it is fixture only.

entries.title: Role with wildcard verbs
entries.why: * on pods includes create, so the pod-creation rule is a true consequence.

entries.title: Role with wildcard resources
entries.why: get on every resource includes get on Secrets and on nodes/proxy, so those rules are true consequences.

entries.title: God-mode role (*, *, *)
entries.why: (*, *, *) grants every verb on every resource, so each specific rule is a true consequence.

entries.title: cluster-admin bound to the default ServiceAccount
cluster-admin bound to a named user
edit granted to every ServiceAccount in a namespace
Namespaced Role with wildcard verbs
entries.why: * on pods includes create.

entries.title: Least-privilege Role bound to one ServiceAccount
Namespaced Role that can read Secrets
entries.why: Reading Secrets in a namespace is a credential-theft primitive.
entries.gap_reason: rbac-secret-read-broad only inspects ClusterRoles by design
entries.would_detect_with: extend the rule to Roles and report namespace-scoped blast radius

entries.title: Kubernetes dashboard exposed
entries.why: An exposed dashboard is also a NodePort Service.

entries.title: ClusterIP Service, LoadBalancer with source ranges, Ingress with TLS
Secret injected through an environment variable
ConfigMap holding an API key in a value
Cloud credentials file mounted into the pod
etcd encryption at rest not enabled
entries.why: The API server runs without --encryption-provider-config.

entries.title: Secret consumed as a read-only file; benign ConfigMap
ConfigMap key containing the word 'token' that is not a credential
entries.why: 'max_tokens' is an LLM sampling limit. A keyword rule matches 'token'.

entries.title: Plaintext credentials stored in a Secret object
entries.why: Secret values are never read by the scanner, on purpose.
entries.gap_reason: the scanner does not read Secret contents (least privilege)
entries.would_detect_with: secret scanning at commit time (gitleaks) or an admission policy

entries.title: Long-lived ServiceAccount token stored as a Secret
entries.why: A non-expiring token that never rotates.
entries.gap_reason: no rule inspects Secret type or token age
entries.would_detect_with: list Secrets by type (metadata only) and flag service-account-token

entries.title: One ServiceAccount reused by 3 workloads across 2 namespaces
entries.why: A compromise of any one inherits the identity of all.

entries.title: A ServiceAccount used by only two workloads
API server has no audit policy
No in-cluster log collector
entries.why: Logs exist only on the node; clearing them leaves no copy.

entries.title: Healthy control plane flags and a log collector
Image with known CVEs (nginx 1.14.0)
entries.why: A pinned tag that is nonetheless years out of date.
entries.gap_reason: no image/CVE scanner runs in the offline fixture
entries.would_detect_with: run with --live --grype (Grype on the running image digests)

entries.title: Image pulled from an untrusted public registry
entries.why: Not from the organisation's registry, not signed, no digest.
entries.gap_reason: no registry allow-list or signature check

entries.title: CronJob that downloads and runs a script
entries.why: Classic persistence. Statically it is just a command line.
entries.gap_reason: no static rule inspects commands; the dedicated rule was removed in the scope reduction

entries.title: Mutating webhook that fails open and injects a sidecar
entries.why: An external webhook that can rewrite every pod, and fails open.
entries.gap_reason: the admission-control rules were removed in the scope reduction
entries.would_detect_with: restore the admission rules (evidence is still collected)

entries.title: No ResourceQuota, LimitRange or PodDisruptionBudget
entries.why: A single tenant can exhaust the node, and a drain can take the app down.
entries.gap_reason: the scanner now READS these kinds but has no rule on them

entries.title: Internet -> Service -> privileged Pod -> ServiceAccount -> Secrets
entries.why: The slide's scenario: reachable from the Internet, runs privileged, and its identity can read every Secret.

entries.title: Same flaw, but not reachable: isolated privileged workload
entries.why: Identical to ap-frontend minus the exposure and the identity. It must rank BELOW it.

entries.title: Same vulnerable image as GAP-IMG1, but Internet-exposed
entries.why: Identical image to the isolated gap-cve-image, behind a LoadBalancer. With --grype its CVE finding must rank ABOVE the isolated one.

entries.title: A fully hardened workload (every pod-security control on)

runtime.title: Shell in the privileged frontend
runtime.why: names a pod of ap-frontend, which has Execution-tagged findings

runtime.title: Read /etc/shadow in a pod with an auto-mounted token
runtime.why: names a pod of wl-sa-automount (Credential Access)

runtime.title: Shell in a pod the scan has never seen
runtime.why: same namespace and tactic as real findings, but no resource-level link

runtime.title: Shell in a cluster whose scan found nothing
runtime.why: the hardened cluster has no static finding of any tactic, so nothing can match

runtime.title: Shell in a clean namespace of a cluster with other findings
runtime.why: documented behaviour: same tactic elsewhere in the cluster is corroborated, not runtime-only (core/correlation.py). Whether that is too generous is a design question.

runtime.title: Pod name that only shares a prefix with a flaw
